extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, academics, and educated public)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and reviewing scientific books, monographs, and reports for a general-science journal, focusing on methods, presentation, completeness, and practical usefulness to target audiences (practitioners and researchers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, simple guidance for practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: If science is to have its due appreciation it must supply information of a practical and simple kind which will appeal to workers in a field already so wide that they have little time for the study of theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific research (e.g., acoustics) intended to influence design and construction should present results in a form readily usable by practitioners (architects, constructors). Avoid excessive theoretical exposition when the target audience requires actionable, easily absorbed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of dedicated laboratory research
rubrics_metrics.description: In this building, devoted solely to acoustic problems, the difficulties of adequate sound transmission and suppression are constantly being investigated. Work of this nature must eventually prove a valuable national asset by preventing wasted effort and expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized experimental facilities that focus on a problem domain (e.g., acoustics lab) are important; they enable systematic investigation of practical problems and produce results that can save time and money when communicated to practitioners and policy-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient sample size and taxonomic/geographic coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation covered ... records were obtained from 1,558 individuals of 327 species ... previously published records from 89 others ... definite statements may be found ... regarding 416 species of birds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting biological measurements, provide clear counts of individuals and species, and indicate geographic and seasonal limits. Large sample sizes and broad taxonomic coverage strengthen generality; state explicitly what is and is not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate measurement instruments and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specially constructed thermometers of the clinical type but with a wider range—95°F+ to 115°F+—were used. When a bird was shot a temperature reading was taken ... only when the specimen could be secured immediately. If there was any delay ... a correct reading could not be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instruments suited to the expected measurement range and ensure measurement timing/protocols preserve validity (e.g., measure immediately to avoid artefactual heat loss). Describe instrument specs and measurement procedures so others can assess reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit and accessibility of raw data
rubrics_metrics.description: A table giving the individual records in detail, not included because of the high cost of printing, is deposited in the files of the Smithsonian Institution of Washington, and may be consulted by those interested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When print constraints prevent full data inclusion, deposit detailed raw data in an accessible institutional archive and state how it can be consulted. This preserves transparency and allows verification and reanalysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limitations and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: It was only possible to secure records from less than half the birds collected. In the short time that intervened ... it is assumed that no appreciable loss of heat from the body took place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly report limitations (e.g., missing data, selection effects) and any assumptions made to interpret measurements. Discuss potential biases caused by incomplete measurements and how they might affect conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate choice of metrics for comparative conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree of heat control of any species is not to be measured by the actual height of the body temperature, but rather by its diurnal variation; according to this standard the regulation of body temperature appears to have reached its highest point in Homo sapiens ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and justify the metric most relevant to the question (e.g., use diurnal range rather than absolute temperature to judge quality of temperature regulation). Avoid drawing broad conclusions based on inappropriate or misleading indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability and pedagogical bridging in laboratory manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The work is the outcome of a particular course of practical lessons ... the device [introductions and summaries] and the general nature of the first four chapters disguise—but do not dispose of—the evils of the type system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratory manuals should be adaptable beyond the originating course, and should bridge lecture principles and lab observations (e.g., via introductions and summaries). Beware overly specialised structure that limits usability in other teaching contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear procedural instructions and comprehensive subject coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The instructions for dissection are clear and sufficient; ... Only one notable omission has been detected: Mr. Hyman’s classification of the Chordates—two pages in length—ignores the Dipnoan fishes, nor in the whole of his book do they once appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, sufficient step-by-step procedures for practical work and ensure comprehensive coverage of relevant taxa/topics demanded by the subject. Omissions of significant groups or procedures reduce the utility and credibility of a manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worked examples and sufficient explanatory detail in technical texts
rubrics_metrics.description: A very good feature is the inclusion of plenty of typical analyses. The book will be found very valuable to students ... Although the quoted results of water analyses are given with the acids and bases combined, there is no indication as to how the necessary calculations are to be made, and some of the sections are so condensed that it is doubtful if they are of value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include worked examples and show explicit calculation steps for typical analyses; avoid over-condensing essential explanatory material. Tailor level of detail to audience needs (e.g., students preparing for exams require stepwise explanations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, clarity and modernity of illustrative materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this book is not clear. The illustrations are found in most text-books with adequate descriptions—those supplied in the present work are often too brief ... Many of the diagrams represent apparatus far from 'modern.' ... descriptions are faulty: Bunsen's eudiometer is ascribed to Cavendish; the Almaden process ... called 'Distillation of mercury.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations and diagrams should have a clear purpose, be up-to-date, and be accompanied by accurate, sufficiently detailed captions/explanations. Ensure factual correctness and correct historical attributions to avoid misleading or confusing readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and revision in textbook editions
rubrics_metrics.description: The sixth edition ... has undergone a revision which brings it completely up-to-date; the section on insanity has been rewritten on the basis of modern psychiatrical views; and that on toxicology gives additional information on poisoning by salvarsan, tetrachlorethane, T.N.T., and the gases of warfare ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks should be revised to incorporate recent developments, modern perspectives, and newly relevant hazards or treatments. Indicate what has been updated so readers can assess currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection standards and indexing for proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The society insists on a high standard of excellence in everything it prints, and the inclusion of a paper in the Proceedings is a sufficient guarantee of quality. The method of indexing each individual volume of the Proceedings leaves nothing to be desired ... suggest that the time is approaching when the Council should consider the desirability of publishing a further subject index to the later volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain rigorous editorial standards for inclusion in society proceedings; provide robust indexing (individual-volume and cumulative subject indexes) to increase accessibility and scholarly utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive analysis and practical policy recommendations in market studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The book analyzes marketing and distribution, instances what has been done in the past and states the present position. The part played by the middleman and dealer is made clear, and the rise of collective bargaining is illustrated ... The producers must also submit to regulations governing their combined action, otherwise the results are doomed to failure. ... the method of arriving at a basic price can only be a starting-point in negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market/policy studies should: (1) analyze institutional roles (middlemen, distributors), (2) examine historical case studies (e.g., strikes, boycotts), (3) discuss regulatory and organizational constraints (perishability, collective action), and (4) offer practical, nuanced recommendations rather than simplistic formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitness and testability in conceptual expositions
rubrics_metrics.description: We would ask our lecturer to give us a sequel to this discourse in which, assuming the four-dimensional presentation, he would state explicitly, either in general terms or by precise illustration, how he would compare the intervals between any two pairs of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting high-level conceptual frameworks (e.g., four-dimensional world views), authors/lecturers should provide explicit, concrete procedures or illustrations showing how their concepts would be tested or operationalized. Avoid sweeping metaphors that cannot be rendered into measurable procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal submission and correspondence policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor does not hold himself responsible for opinions expressed by his correspondents. Neither can he undertake to return, or to correspond with the writers of, rejected manuscripts intended for this or any other part of NATURE. No notice is taken of anonymous communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should state clear submission policies: disclaim editorial responsibility for letters' opinions, specify that rejected manuscripts will not be returned or receive correspondence, and that anonymous communications will not be considered. Make these policies explicit to manage contributor expectations.
